Pantomime

PAN-tuh-mym -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, PAN. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pantomime is expressing meaning through gesture.

Rather than shout across the silent reading room, the twins invented a private pantomime for 'meet me outside.'

Worked Example

The street performer never says a word, yet the crowd follows an entire story: her hands build an invisible wall, her shoulders sag against an imaginary wind, and when she finally 'opens' a door that is not there, the whole plaza cheers.

That performance is pantomime: expressing meaning entirely through gesture, without speech. The word covers both the everyday act -- miming 'water' across a loud room -- and the theatrical art of telling whole stories in silent movement.

How Pantomime Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

mime

mime: acting out meaning silently with the body

gesturing

gesturing: using hand and body movements to communicate

Antonyms

speech

speech: communication through spoken words

narration

narration: telling a story aloud in words

How Strong Is It? — gesturing → pantomime → mime

gesturing vs. pantomime

gesturing vs. pantomime: Gesturing is the loose, everyday word -- a wave or a shrug is a gesture -- while pantomime organizes gestures into a full message or story that needs no words at all.

mime vs. pantomime

mime vs. pantomime: Mime is the strongest match: both mean silent acting, but mime usually names the trained art or the artist, while pantomime covers any wordless acting-out, from a stage show to charades at a birthday party.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — panto-

root — panto-: all, every (Greek pantos)

root — mime

root — mime: imitator, actor (Greek mimos)

Put it together

Put it together: Pantomime is Greek for 'imitator of everything' -- pantos ('all') plus mimos ('imitator'). In Roman theaters, a pantomime was a single performer who acted out every role in a story without speaking; the word now names that whole art of meaning made from gesture alone.

Use the root in a new word: mimic

Use the root in a new word: mimic: The parrot can mimic the doorbell so well that the dog falls for it every time.

Root Check

Word Choice

Pantomime works two ways: as the silent communication itself ('she used pantomime to order lunch abroad') and as a theatrical performance told through gesture. Either way, the defining rule is NO words -- if someone is talking while waving their arms, it is just gesturing, not pantomime.
